scientific_question: For each root-free frozen rational snapshot, how large a simultaneous coefficient box, scaled by local linearized standard errors, can be certified root-free over the entire held-out closed interval by exact rational arithmetic?

parameter_box_rule.box: For every nonconstant denominator coefficient c_j, allow |delta c_j| <= rho * sigma_j, where sigma_j is the frozen local linearized standard error
parameter_box_rule.scale_scope: Sigma is only a local sensitivity scale; the box is not a confidence ellipsoid, probability region, measurement uncertainty or physical endogeneity claim
parameter_box_rule.sufficient_condition: Choose sign s from the snapshot denominator at the lower endpoint. If s*D(x)-rho*sum(sigma_j*|x|^j)>0 for every x in the closed interval, then every coefficient in the box is root-free there
parameter_box_rule.interval_sign: Require each held-out interval to be entirely nonnegative or entirely nonpositive in x so |x|^j is polynomial with the appropriate sign
parameter_box_rule.exactness: Use exact rational coefficients and Sturm root counts; do not replace the continuous box proof with sampled perturbation points

radius_search_rule.lower_bound: Largest tested radius certified by the sufficient condition; every coefficient in that entire box is root-free
radius_search_rule.upper_bound: Smallest tested radius not satisfying the sufficient certificate; do not call it unsafe or a true maximum
radius_search_rule.cap_hit: If radius 4 is certified, report a capped lower bound of 4 and do not claim it is maximal
radius_search_rule.rooted_snapshot: If the snapshot already has a root, no positive root-free box exists; report snapshot_safe=false rather than running a radius search

prohibitions: No refitting, standard-error recomputation or interval retuning
No interpretation of the sufficient radius as a necessary radius, confidence level or exact physical tolerance
No claim that the uncertified upper bracket is unsafe
No global root-free claim outside the specified box and closed x interval
